elements.quote: Occurrence and transmission potential of asymptomatic and presymptomatic SARSCoV-2 infections: A living systematic review and meta-analysis
elements.reason: The title explicitly identifies the report as a 'living systematic review and meta-analysis'.

elements.quote: Occurrence and transmission potential of asymptomatic and presymptomatic SARSCoV-2 infections
elements.reason: The title provides key information about the population (asymptomatic and presymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infections) and the objective (occurrence and transmission potential).

elements.quote: A living systematic review and meta-analysis
elements.reason: The title provides supplementary information regarding the update status by explicitly stating it is a 'living systematic review'.

elements.quote: There is disagreement about the level of asymptomatic severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection.
elements.reason: The Background section explicitly describes the current state of knowledge (disagreement) and uncertainties regarding asymptomatic infection levels.

elements.quote: The amount, and infectiousness, of asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection will determine what kind of measures will prevent transmission most effectively.
elements.reason: The Author Summary explains the importance and need for the review by linking the knowledge to the effectiveness of prevention measures.

elements.quote: We found three systematic reviews, which reported similar summary estimates from meta-analysis of studies published up to May [119-121]. In comparison with other reviews, rather than restricting inclusion, we give a comprehensive overview of studies with adequate follow-up...
elements.reason: The text identifies existing systematic reviews and explains the need for the current review by highlighting its comprehensive approach and focus on adequate follow-up.
The review focuses on the proportion of asymptomatic infection and transmission dynamics, not on intervention effects, so a mechanism of action is not applicable.
The review is observational/epidemiological regarding infection status, not a complex intervention, so a logic model is not applicable.

elements.quote: The objectives of this study were to address three questions: (1) Amongst people who become infected with SARS-CoV-2, what proportion do not experience symptoms at all during their infection? (2) Amongst people with SARS-CoV-2 infection who are asymptomatic when diagnosed, what proportion will develop symptoms later? (3) What proportion of SARS-CoV-2 transmission is accounted for by people who are either asymptomatic throughout infection or presymptomatic?
elements.reason: The Introduction section explicitly states the three review questions/objectives using a clear question format.

elements.quote: The objectives of this study were to address three questions: (1) Amongst people who become infected with SARS-CoV-2, what proportion do not experience symptoms at all during their infection? (2) Amongst people with SARS-CoV-2 infection who are asymptomatic when diagnosed, what proportion will develop symptoms later? (3) What proportion of SARS-CoV-2 transmission is accounted for by people who are either asymptomatic throughout infection or presymptomatic?
elements.reason: The review addresses epidemiological proportions and transmission dynamics rather than intervention effects, so PICO comparisons are not applicable.

elements.quote: Weincluded studies in any language of people with SARS-CoV-2 diagnosed by RT-PCR that documented follow-up and symptom status at the beginning and end of follow-up or investigated the contribution to SARS-CoV-2 transmission of asymptomatic or presymptomatic infection. elements.quote: We found narrative reviews that reported wide ranges (5%-96%) of infections that might be asymptomatic [1,118]. These reviews presented cross-sectional studies alongside longitudinal studies and did not distinguish between asymptomatic and presymptomatic infection. We found three systematic reviews, which reported similar summary estimates from meta-analysis of studies published up to May [119-121]. ... In comparison with other reviews, rather than restricting inclusion, we give a comprehensive overview of studies with adequate follow-up, with assessment of risks of bias and exploration of heterogeneity (S2-S7 Figs).
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly compares the review's findings with other narrative and systematic reviews in the 'Comparison With Other Reviews' section, interpreting the results in the context of existing evidence.

elements.quote: Limitations of the review are that most included studies were not designed to estimate the proportion of asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection and definitions of asymptomatic status were often incomplete or absent. The risks of bias, particularly those affecting selection of participants, differed between studies and could result in both underestimation and overestimation of the true proportion of asymptomatic infections. Also, we did not consider the possible impact of false negative RT-PCR results, which might be more likely to occur in asymptomatic infections [116] and would underestimate the proportion of asymptomatic infections [117].
elements.reason: The text explicitly discusses limitations of the evidence included in the review, including study design issues, selection bias risks, false negative RT-PCR impacts, and database coverage.
